text: Ichabod lived. <break time="0.8s" /> With the families of his students. <break time="0.8s" /> Staying a week at each house. <break time="0.8s" /> In turn. <break time="0.8s" /> He helped with the farm work. <break time="0.8s" /> Taught singing on Sundays. <break time="0.8s" /> And was popular. <break time="0.8s" /> With the women of the valley. <break time="0.8s" /> He loved ghost stories. <break time="0.8s" /> And on winter evenings. <break time="0.8s" /> He listened to the old wives tales. <break time="0.8s" /> Until he trembled. <break time="0.8s" /> Walking home in the dark afterward. <break time="0.8s" /> He jumped at every shadow. <break time="0.8s" /> And sang loudly. <break time="0.8s" /> To keep up his courage. <break time="0.8s" /> Among his singing students. <break time="0.8s" /> Was Katrina Van Tassel. <break time="0.8s" /> The only daughter. <break time="0.8s" /> Of a very rich Dutch farmer. <break time="0.8s" /> She was eighteen. <break time="0.8s" /> With rosy cheeks. <break time="0.8s" /> And she was famous. <break time="0.8s" /> For both her beauty and her fathers money. <break time="0.8s" /> When Ichabod saw the fat pigs, turkeys. <break time="0.8s" /> And wide fields. <break time="0.8s" /> Of the Van Tassel farm. <break time="0.8s" /> His eyes shone. <break time="0.8s" /> If I married Katrina. <break time="0.8s" /> All of this would be mine. <break time="0.8s" /> He thought. <break time="0.8s" /> Picturing every pig. <break time="0.8s" /> As a roast dinner. <break time="0.8s" /> But Ichabod had a rival. <break time="0.8s" /> Brom Bones. <break time="0.8s" /> The strongest young man in the valley. <break time="0.8s" /> And its best horseman. <break time="0.8s" /> Brom loved pranks. <break time="0.8s" /> And whenever his horse was tied. <break time="0.8s" /> At the Van Tassels fence. <break time="0.8s" /> Other young men stayed away.
